newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBS FORGE UPWARDS TO END TOKYO DAY FIRMER.
newsitem.headline: JGBS FORGE UPWARDS TO END TOKYO DAY FIRMER.

text.p: The benchmark 10-year September Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract forged upwards to end Thursday trade sharply higher, mainly on short-covering sparked by weaker stocks, traders said.

Loss-cut selling of construction stocks, prompted by the fact share prices were showing no signs of recovery, helped take the Nikkei down to its lowest close since May 1, at 19,475.85, down 226.22 points, providing bond traders with an excuse to cover short positions.
Key September closed at 126.50, up from 126.10 at Wednesday's close, with turnover of 38,259.

With activity thinned as operators took summer vacations, the key September moved volatilely from 126.04 to 126.55. But traders attributed this mainly to the Nikkei's moves, along with book-squaring and bargain-hunting.

"Right now trade tends to be controlled mostly by day traders taking advantage of the market's moves, with few wanting to slant their portfolios strongly in either direction," one trust bank trader said.
Morning trade began relatively strongly after a large buying order came in from a major Japanese city bank, which bought again later at 126.40, a securities firm trader said.

September then hovered around this level for much of the afternoon as selling lined up from 126.46-126.50, but late weakness in stocks prompted a spurt of short-covering and took the key contract higher.

Although some traders said concerns about the health of second-tier construction firms was supplying additional support for bonds, others said this was peripheral at best. "It's not as if this is new talk, after all. But by pushing stocks lower, this has helped bonds climb," one said.
Yields on straight bonds issued by these firms were higher in the corporate bond market on Thursday, traders said.

Fujita Corp's 3.0 percent straight bond due September 2001, rated triple B minus by the Japan Bond Research Institute (JBRI), was offered at a yield of 9.77 percent, more than 800 basis points above the four-year interest-rate swap (IRS) rate of around 1.55/1.59 percent, traders said.
The Fujita bond was offered at 9.43 percent on late Wednesday.
Some buying of longer-term cash bonds was detected in morning trade, probably by investors, although the volume most likely was not large, traders said. Even so, this helped push futures higher.
Yield on the benchmark 182nd 10-year cash bond was at 2.115 percent at 0637 GMT against 2.155 percent at Wednesday's close. It moved between 2.110 and 2.165 percent during the day.
Traders said the market is waiting for Friday's release of Japanese June machinery orders, due out at 0500 GMT. But even so, the impact is likely to be limited.
